question: The mode and median of a data is 26.7 and 71, respectively. What is the mean of the data? (Use empirical formula.)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply **Empirical Formula**: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

26.7 = 3 × 71 − 2 × **Mean**

2 × **Mean** = 213 − 26.7 = 186.3

**Mean** = 186.3 ÷ 2 = 93.15

**∴ The correct answer is 93.15.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mode** = 26.7

**Median** = 71

**Formula Used:**

The relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is given by: **Mode** = 3(**Median**) − 2(**Mean**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4899f00bee04d0dbe6e962786882077673e256e6c92a0b2634171f1a261ddf0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 26.7 = 3(71) − 2(**Mean**)

⇒ 26.7 = 213 − 2 × **Mean**

⇒ 2 × **Mean** = 213 − 26.7

⇒ 2 × **Mean** = 186.3

⇒ **Mean** = 186.3 ÷ 2

⇒ **Mean** = 93.15

**∴ The correct answer is 93.15.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

It is an approximate relationship used for moderately skewed distributions: **Mean** − **Mode** = 3(**Mean** − **Median**).

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all identical (**Mean** = **Median** = **Mode**).

Skewness and Mean

In a **positively skewed** distribution, **Mean** > **Median** > **Mode**. In a **negatively skewed** distribution, **Mean** < **Median** < **Mode**.</p
